Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR  

| Shield type | Image-ID that the style looks for | Example IDs that **must** exist in a sprite |
|-------------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| US Interstate | `us-interstate_{ref_length}` | `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3`, `us-interstate_4`, `us-interstate_5` |
| US Highway   | `us-highway_{ref_length}`   | `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3` |
| US State     | `us-state_{ref_length}`     | `us-state_1`, `us-state_2`, `us-state_3`, `us-state_4`, `us-state_5`, `us-state_6` |
| Generic road | `road_{ref_length}`         | `road_1`, `road_2`, `road_3`, `road_4`, `road_5`, `road_6` |

The **only thing** you need to make the badges appear is to have a sprite (or a second sprite sheet) that contains those exact IDs. You do **not** have to touch any layer definitions.

---

## 1. Why the numbers appear but the badge does not

* The text part of a shield (`text-field: "{ref}"`) is rendered from the **glyphs** server – that works fine, which is why you see the numbers.
* The badge behind the number is drawn from the **sprite** via the `icon-image` property.  
  In the OSM-Bright / OSM-Liberty styles the `icon-image` is an **expression** that expands to the string `"{network}_{ref_length}"`.  
  When the sprite does not contain an entry with that exact ID, the style manager fires `styleimagemissing` and the icon is omitted, leaving only the number.

So the fix is simply “**provide the missing sprite entries**”.

---

## 2. Exact sprite image names the built-in shield layers request

The three shield layers in the default OSM-Bright style (and the single shield layer in OSM-Liberty) use the following layout:

```json
{
  "id": "highway-shield-us-interstate",
  "type": "symbol",
  "source": "transportation_name",
  "layout": {
    "icon-image": "{network}_{ref_length}",
    "text-field": "{ref}"
  }
}
```

* `network` is a property on the tile data. For US roads it is one of:
  * `"us-interstate"` → badge IDs `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, …  
  * `"us-highway"`   → badge IDs `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3`
  * `"us-state"`     → badge IDs `us-state_1` … `us-state_6`
* For non-US roads the style falls back to the generic `road` network, so the IDs are `road_1` … `road_6`.

The `{ref_length}` property is an integer (1-6) that tells the style how many digits the road number has; the style simply concatenates it to the network name with an underscore.

**Therefore the sprite **must** contain every combination listed in the table above** (or at least the ones that actually occur in your data). If a particular length is never used you can omit that entry, but the IDs that *do* appear must be present.

---

## 3. Getting the badges without editing any layers  

You have three practical ways to supply those IDs:

### 3.1 Point the style at a sprite that already contains them  

The OSM-Bright sprite hosted by OpenMapTiles includes **all** of the IDs listed above.

```json
{
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite"
}
```

*If you are already using a different basemap style that ships its own sprite, you can replace the `sprite` URL with the one above.*  
All other icons in the original sprite will be lost, so you normally do this only if you control the whole style.

### 3.2 Add a **second sprite sheet** that only contains the shield badges  

Since MapLibre GL JS 3.0 you can have **multiple sprite sheets** in a single style. Keep the original (default) sprite for all the other POI icons, and add a second sheet that only holds the shield images.

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://example.com/your-original-sprite" },
    { "id": "shields",  "url": "https://example.com/shield-sprite" }
  ]
}
```

* The shield sprite (`shield-sprite`) must contain the IDs exactly as listed (`us-interstate_1`, …, `road_6`).  
* Because the style’s `icon-image` expression does **not** include a prefix, you need to make the shield sheet the **default** one, or you must rename the IDs in the expression. The easiest way is to **make the shield sheet the default**:

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://example.com/shield-sprite" },
    { "id": "extra",   "url": "https://example.com/your-original-sprite" }
  ]
}
```

Now the existing `icon-image` expression (`"{network}_{ref_length}"`) resolves against the default sheet and finds the badge images, while all other icons continue to resolve against the `extra` sheet (they must be referenced with the `extra:` prefix, e.g. `"icon-image": "extra:park"`).

If you cannot edit the style JSON (e.g., you are consuming a third-party style at runtime), you can add the second sheet **programmatically** after the style loads:

```js
map.on('style.load', () => {
  // Add the shield sheet as the default (first entry)
  map.addSprite('default', 'https://example.com/shield-sprite');
  // Add the original sheet under another id, if you still need its icons
  map.addSprite('extra', 'https://example.com/your-original-sprite');
});
```

> **Note:** `addSprite` can only be called *after* the style’s `load` event. The first call creates the default sheet; subsequent calls add additional sheets.

### 3.3 Register the missing images at runtime with `addImage`

If you prefer not to touch the style’s `sprite` property at all, you can load the badge PNGs (or SVGs) yourself and register them with the map **once the style has loaded**:

```js
async function addShield(id, url) {
  const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);   // PNG/WebP/JPEG only
  if (!map.hasImage(id)) map.addImage(id, data);
}

// Example for the US-Interstate 2-digit badge
addShield('us-interstate_2', 'https://example.com/shields/us-interstate_2.png');
addShield('us-highway_1',    'https://example.com/shields/us-highway_1.png');
// …repeat for every id you need
```

*If you have SVG badge files you must rasterise them first (create an `Image` element, wait for `onload`, then `addImage`).*  
Because the style already asks for those IDs, once you register them the map will instantly start drawing the badges—no layer changes required.

**Pros / Cons**

| Method | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| Replace `sprite` URL | One-shot, no extra code | Loses any other icons that were in the original sprite |
| Multiple sprite sheets | Keeps original icons, only adds shields | Requires the style to use the `default` sheet for shields or to prefix other icons |
| `addImage` at runtime | No style changes, works with any existing sprite | You must manually load every badge you need (more network requests) and you lose the automatic `@2x` handling unless you provide both resolutions yourself |

Pick the approach that best fits your deployment constraints.

---

## 4. Quick checklist – “Why is my shield still missing?”

1. **Open the browser console** → you should see a warning like  
   `Image "us-interstate_3" could not be loaded`.  
   That tells you exactly which ID is missing.
2. **Verify the sprite JSON** you are using (e.g. `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json`). Search for the missing ID. If it isn’t there → you need a different sprite or to add the image yourself.
3. **CORS** – the sprite JSON and PNG must be served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or your domain). Otherwise the map will silently fail to load the image.
4. **@2x variants** – if you are on a high-DPI screen and the sprite only provides `*_1.png` but not `*_1@2x.png`, the map will fall back to the 1× version, which is fine. If you want crisp high-DPI badges, provide the `@2x` PNGs in the same folder.

---

## 5. Example: Minimal “shield-only” sprite

If you only need the badges and want to keep your existing sprite untouched, create a tiny sprite directory:

```
shield-sprite/
├─ shield-sprite.png          (atlas with all badge PNGs)
├─ shield-sprite@2x.png       (optional high-DPI version)
└─ shield-sprite.json         (index)
```

`shield-sprite.json` (excerpt):

```json
{
  "us-interstate_1": { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 0,   "y": 0,   "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-interstate_2": { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 24,  "y": 0,   "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-interstate_3": { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 48,  "y": 0,   "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-highway_1":    { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 0,   "y": 24,  "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-highway_2":    { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 24,  "y": 24,  "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-highway_3":    { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 48,  "y": 24,  "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "us-state_1":      { "width": 24, "height": 24, "x": 0,   "y": 48,  "pixelRatio": 1 },
  "...":            { ... }
}
```

Host it (e.g. on a CDN or your own static file server) and point the style’s `sprite` entry to `https://mycdn.example.com/shield-sprite/shield-sprite`. The style will now find the badges and render full shields.

---

## 6. One-liner for most users

> **If you are using the default OSM-Bright style from OpenMapTiles, just replace the `sprite` URL with the official one:**

```json
{
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite"
}
```

That sprite contains **all** `us-interstate_*`, `us-highway_*`, `us-state_*`, and `road_*` images, so the shields appear automatically and you don’t need any code changes.
